thread:
sam.peopleops: Heads up 1 — employee lost their physical insurance card while transiting through SFO, had to use urgent care (Claim UC-1182) this morning. Provider is saying claim paid OON because their billing TIN didn't match the insurer file. Member has prior auth PA-4450 for the episode. Theyre leaving the country tonight and need a digital proof of coverage and quick steps to get the claim reprocessed. Any fast wins?

mira.benefits: Short checklist: 1) temp proof-of-coverage PDF for scheduling/verification; 2) ask provider to resubmit with the rendering provider NPI and billing TIN that matches insurer file, include PA-4450 in claim remarks; 3) member uploads EOB + itemized receipt to benefits portal so we can open escalation.

devon.hr: Member is very stressed. Can we include explicit script text the clinic can copy into the claim resubmission and a one-sentence script for check-in so they don't cancel remaining meds?

travel-liaison: For travel cases, schedulers often need a one-page attestation and the insurer phone number. If urgent care needs proof to waive up-front payment, they may accept the digital PDF plus the insurer phone. If not, member may have to pay and pursue reimbursement.

mira.benefits: Suggested claim resubmission note for the clinic: "Please reprocess claim UC-1182: Prior Authorization PA-4450 applies. Correct billing provider NPI and billing TIN to match insurer provider file; denial due to provider credential/billing entity mismatch. Attach itemized bill and PA documentation. Mark for reconsideration/reprocessing." Have them populate box 23/claim remark with `PA-4450`.

benefits-bot: Draft temporary proof-of-coverage (informational only): "Redwood Inference 1 Temporary Proof of Coverage. Member: [NAME]. Member ID: [MASKED_ID]. Plan: Redwood Core PPO. Coverage period: 01/01/2026 - 12/31/2026. Prior Authorization: PA-4450 (urgent care visit). For immediate claim inquiries, call insurer provider relations 1-800-555-0199 or submit a provider portal case at provider.insurer.example.com. This document does not guarantee payment. Please confirm billing provider NPI/TIN matches insurer provider file before resubmission."

insurer-bot: If provider resubmits with corrected billing credentials and attaches PA-4450 and the itemized invoice, we can re-open claim UC-1182 for reprocessing. If provider gives a different billing entity, request that they include the contracted rendering NPI. Escalation path: open provider relations case referencing claim UC-1182 + PA-4450 and include EOB and itemized bill.

devon.hr: Could benefits draft the one-liner the member can read to the clinic at check-in? Something like: "I have active coverage under Redwood Core PPO and prior authorization PA-4450 for today's visit; please verify billing NPI/TIN and resubmit under the contracted provider billing entity."

mira.benefits: Yep — use: "I have active Redwood Core PPO coverage. Please accept this temporary proof of coverage and confirm billing provider NPI/TIN matches insurer provider file; prior auth PA-4450 applies."

travel-liaison: Also tell the member to snap photos of receipts, sign any financial responsibility forms if they must pay, and immediately upload to the benefits portal. That speeds reimbursement and escalation.

mira.benefits: I'll prepare the PDF, DM the member, and post the resubmission note for the clinic. Once the provider confirms resubmission, I'll open a provider relations escalation and attach PA-4450 + EOB. If insurer denies again, escalate to medical appeals with clinical notes and prior auth documentation.

sam.peopleops: Awesome, thank you. I'll ping the member and update here after they get the PDF. :thumbsup:
